title: Strict tensor towers compute diagram-derived reduction with the specified transitions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $S_\bullet=(S_n,s_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n)_{n\ge1}$ a strict tower of unital commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-inverse-system]. Use the ringed diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], module sheaves, unbounded derived localizations $Q$, and flat-term K-flat complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Fix derived tensor and its two-sided K-flat comparison as in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and the one-sided normalization [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization]. Whenever $P$ and $\Delta P$ are flat-term K-flat, there is a normalized isomorphism in the derived category of strict $R$-module towers
$$c_{P,S}:\Delta(QP)\otimes^L_{\Delta R}S_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(T_S(P)),\qquad T_S(P)_n=P\otimes_RS_n.$$
Here $\Delta(QP)$ means the derived functor of exact diagonal applied to $QP$. The complex tower $T_S(P)$ has differential $d_P\otimes1$, actual transition $1_P\otimes s_n$, and coefficient-map components $1_P\otimes a_n$ for every algebra-tower morphism $a:S_\bullet\to T_\bullet$. The displayed comparison is natural in homotopy-category maps of the resolving complex and in coefficient-tower maps. Its evaluation agrees with the one-sided tensor computation on $\mathcal C$ conjugated by the exact-evaluation localization comparisons, and the ordinary evaluation maps are identity on local pure tensors. In particular the evaluation identifications commute with the strict transitions before localization.
For $V\in\mathcal C$, put $R_V=R|_V$ and let $J_R$ be exact termwise slice extension [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, def-sf-strict-tensor-reduction-termwise]. If $P$ on $\mathcal C/V$, $j_{R!}P$, and both constant diagrams are flat-term K-flat, the comparisons above and exact-extension localization give
$$\mathcal R_S(j_{R!}QP)\cong Q(T_S(j_{R!}P)),\qquad J_R\mathcal R_{S|_V}(QP)\cong Q(J_RT_{S|_V}(P)),$$
where $\mathcal R_S(M)=\Delta M\otimes^L_{\Delta R}S_\bullet$. These identifications are natural in both variables and have the same evaluated normalization. No K-flatness or flatness of $S_\bullet$, nor surjectivity of its transitions, is assumed.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and identify $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ with modules over $\Delta R$ on the small diagram site by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Write $Q_d,Q_c$ for diagram and base localization. The levelwise kernels and cokernels of [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] show that $\Delta$ is exact: applying it gives the constant diagrams on the original kernel and cokernel. Evaluation $e_n$ is exact by the diagram-site lemma. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to fix natural localization comparisons $d_P:\Delta_D(Q_cP)\cong Q_d(\Delta P)$ and $\epsilon_{n,A}:E_n(Q_dA)\cong Q_c(e_nA)$. All subsequent conjugations use these comparisons; here $\Delta_D,E_n$ denote the derived exact functors. No diagram in $D(R)$ is substituted for the derived category of strict diagrams.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; exact diagonal and evaluation in the existing diagram-site realization

proof.text: Regard $S_\bullet$ as the degree-zero complex $S_\bullet[0]$. The ordinary tensor on the diagram site is the sheafification of sectionwise tensor. The evaluation inverse images of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] have identity coefficient map, so [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] gives the ordinary evaluation comparison with $p\otimes s\mapsto p\otimes s$. In degree $i$ of $\operatorname{Tot}(\Delta P\otimes_{\Delta R}S_\bullet[0])$ only the summand $(i,0)$ is nonzero. Its differential is $d_P\otimes1$ by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. In the diagram direction the restriction of a sectionwise tensor is the tensor of the two restriction maps; hence it sends $p\otimes s$ at level $n+1$ to $p\otimes s_n(s)$ at level $n$. Sheafification preserves this equality by its universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Thus these comparisons assemble to a cochain isomorphism $\theta_{P,S}:\operatorname{Tot}(\Delta P\otimes_{\Delta R}S_\bullet[0])\cong T_S(P)$ with the specified strict transitions, rather than merely separate derived isomorphisms at each level.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization] on the diagram site with $T=\Delta P$ and $M=S_\bullet[0]$. Its hypotheses hold by the assumed flat terms and K-flatness of $\Delta P$; the second factor is unrestricted. Define, with composition written right to left,
$$c_{P,S}=Q_d(\theta_{P,S})\,c^{d}_{\Delta P,S_\bullet[0]}\,(d_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}1).$$
This is the claimed derived isomorphism. For a homotopy-category map $u:P\to P'$ the second naturality equation of that lemma gives the conjugated map $Q_d(u\otimes1)$; for $a:S_\bullet\to T_\bullet$ its first equation gives $Q_d(1\otimes a)$. The ordinary comparisons in Step 2 are natural in both variables by cochain tensor coherence. Therefore the resulting components on $T_S(P)$ are $u\otimes1$ and $1_P\otimes a_n$, respectively. In particular the comparison is normalized by the specified two-sided derived tensor comparison, not by an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and preceding one-sided construction, with the fixed two-sided normalization

proof.text:
Fix $n$ and use the ringed inverse image $e_n$ of Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], it takes every flat-term K-flat diagram complex to a flat-term K-flat complex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-comparison-descent-representatives] with $F=e_n$, $LF=E_n$, $q=Q_d$, $q'=Q_c$, and counit $\epsilon_n$. The representative tensor isomorphisms are those of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on the two small sites; its full-faithfulness clause supplies the restriction hypothesis. The counit is invertible on every complex by Step 1, hence also on tensors of representatives. The ordinary comparison is the cochain comparison of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. We obtain the normalized natural derived comparison
$$\beta_{n;A,B}:E_n(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}B)\cong E_nA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}E_nB.$$
Its defining representative square says exactly that, on two flat-term K-flat complexes, $\beta_n$ is the localized ordinary tensor evaluation comparison conjugated by their specified two-sided tensor and exact-evaluation comparisons.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product) and 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); representative-square descent by the existing categorical lemma

proof.text:
To verify the same square with the second factor $S_\bullet[0]$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $v:V\to S_\bullet[0]$ on the diagram site using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Exact evaluation carries $v$ to a quasi-isomorphism, and $e_nV$ has flat terms and is K-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. Apply one-sided naturality [lem-trf-site-one-sided-tensor-normalization] to $v$ on both sites. The two-sided representative square in Step 4 gives equality for $(\Delta P,V)$. Naturality of $\beta_n$ and $\epsilon_n$, and the ordinary cochain comparison's naturality, identify the two composites after precomposing with $E_n(1\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q_dv)$. This arrow is invertible; cancel it. Consequently
$$\epsilon_{n,T_S(P)}\,E_n(c_{P,S})=c^c_{P,S_n[0]}\,(\epsilon_{n,\Delta P}\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_{n,S[0]})\,\beta_{n;Q_d\Delta P,Q_dS[0]}\,E_n(d_P\otimes^{\mathbf L}1),$$
where the ordinary evaluation identification of Step 2 is inserted on the left. The diagonal localization and evaluation comparisons also identify $E_n\Delta_D(Q_cP)$ with $Q_cP$. This is precisely the asserted one-sided evaluation normalization, including the exact-localization conjugations.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), and 06YU (definition-derived-tor); agent cancellation verification of normalization

proof.text: For an actual transition, the two routes in the ordinary evaluation square both send $p\otimes s$ to $p\otimes s_n(s)$. For a coefficient-tower map $a$, the corresponding square is the equality $a_ns_n=t_na_{n+1}$ tensored with $1_P$. The maps are linear, and equality on the presheaf tensor generators extends uniquely to the sheaf tensor by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For a chain homotopy $h$, tensoring with a degree-zero coefficient gives $h\otimes1$ and $d(h\otimes1)+(h\otimes1)d=(dh+hd)\otimes1$. Thus the transition and coefficient squares already hold for strict complexes and homotopy-category maps. Localizing these equalities proves their compatibility with the comparisons of Steps 3–5; no faithfulness of derived evaluations is asserted.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product) and 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); direct degree-zero tensor calculation

proof.text:
On the slice site apply Steps 1–5 with $R_V$ and $S_\bullet|_V$. On the base apply them to $j_{R!}P$ and $S_\bullet$. The required four flat-term K-flat hypotheses are exactly those assumed in the statement, so this invokes no unproved preservation property of extension. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] the module extension $j_{R!}$ is exact. By [def-sf-strict-tensor-reduction-termwise] its termwise diagram extension $J_R$ preserves finite limits and colimits. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] supplies $\lambda_A:J_{R,D}Q_{d,V}A\cong Q_d(J_RA)$ and $\xi_P:j_{R!,D}Q_{c,V}P\cong Q_c(j_{R!}P)$. The two requested maps are explicitly
$$c_{j_{R!}P,S}\,\mathcal R_S(\xi_P),\qquad \lambda_{T_{S|_V}(P)}\,J_{R,D}(c_{P,S|_V}).$$
Both are isomorphisms. Exact extension and evaluation commute termwise: at level $n$ both complexes are $j_{R!}(A_n)$ with the same differential. Their localization comparisons therefore agree under this ordinary identity by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Applying Step 5 to these two composites gives their evaluated normalization. Naturality follows from the naturality of every displayed factor. Throughout only the resolving factors, never $S_\bullet$, were required to be flat or K-flat; no step used surjectivity of $s_n$.
